advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Prefer a version-gated skipif (e.g. skip only when git >= 2.47) over an unconditional skip so the prune-locking regression guard still runs where the git-maintenance race does not occur.
evidence: reason text: "git >= 2.47's `git commit` spawns a DETACHED background `git maintenance run --auto` ... that runs OUTSIDE rebar's write lock" — the failure is version-conditional, but the skip is unconditional.
Module docstring (lines 1-19) establishes this test is the guard that 'asserts no write is lost' for bug eclectic-spotted-barb.

Codebase idiom for version/environment-specific disabling is conditional: tests/interfaces/store/test_push_parent_exit.py:37 `pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(os.name != "posix", ...)`; numerous `pytest.mark.skipif(not _SSH_OK, reason="ssh-keygen >= 8.9 required ...")` guards.
advisory.finding: The test is disabled unconditionally with @pytest.mark.skip, but the documented root cause is specific to git >= 2.47 (the git 2.54 CI matrix). This erases the only regression guard for bug eclectic-spotted-barb (unlocked prune racing locked writes) on ALL environments, including git < 2.47 where the maintenance race does not occur and the test would still catch a regression of the prune-locking invariant.
scenarios: Local dev / CI runners on git < 2.47 where the prune-locking regression could reappear undetected.
A future change to _prune_queue_events reintroduces the unlocked-prune bug and no test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace @pytest.mark.skip with @pytest.mark.skipif gated on the detected git version (>= 2.47), keeping the same reason/ownership text, so the invariant is still exercised on unaffected git versions.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the unconditional `@pytest.mark.skip` with an environment-gated `skipif` keyed to the affected git version (or a strict `xfail(strict=True, reason=...)`) so the test still runs and gates on unaffected environments and flips when the bug is fixed.
evidence: `@pytest.mark.skip(reason="TEMPORARILY DISABLED (bug 88eb ...) to unblock CI. This test currently fails on the git 2.54 CI matrix ...")` at test_enrich_drain_prune_concurrency.py:68-76

The condition described is environment-specific (git >= 2.47 / git 2.54 matrix) but the mark used is unconditional `skip`, not `skipif(<git-version-condition>)` — so it also disables the test on environments where the bug does not manifest.

Sibling tests in the same directory gate on the actual environment: `@pytest.mark.skipif(_AGENTS, ...)` (test_llm_optionality.py:92) and `pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(os.name != "posix", ...)` (test_push_parent_exit.py:37) — the environment-dependent form was available and idiomatic here.

The test body is a valid behavioral oracle (`assert swallowed_raises == 0 and disk_total == intended_total` at :137) exercising real multi-process git; skipping it removes coverage of a CONFIRMED data-corruption/lost-write bug.
`show_ticket("88eb-2beb-65f5-4bc0")` -> "Error: rebar show failed (exit 1): Ticket '88eb-2beb-65f5-4bc0' not found"
reason text: "RE-ENABLE (remove this skip) once that fix lands — owned by 88eb" — the owning ticket cannot be located to confirm it tracks removal.
advisory.finding: The regression test for a confirmed, unfixed write-loss bug is disabled with a bare unconditional `@pytest.mark.skip`, which suppresses it in ALL environments — not just the 'git 2.54 CI matrix' the reason names. This is a non-gating suppression: the test can never fail and provides zero regression coverage anywhere.
merged_from: The skip's stated re-enable condition is owned by ticket 88eb-2beb-65f5-4bc0, but that ticket is not resolvable in the tracker, so the removal condition is not externally tracked and the skip risks becoming permanent.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use `@pytest.mark.skipif(<git >= 2.47 detection>, reason=...)` so the test continues to run and gate on git versions that lack the detached-maintenance race, or a `@pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason="bug 88eb: git detached auto-maintenance races the write lock")` so the suite alerts when the fix lands.
